incidental_findings.finding: UNANSWERABLE AS RENDERED - the most serious problem in either set. The peer's work is quoted with the blank still in it: "Rosa solved: 'Starting from 12 and subtracting 2 repeatedly, you subtract ___ times before reaching 0'." Rosa's answer is never shown, yet the key asserts has_error=True. There is nothing on the page for the pupil to find an error in. Looks like the error-finding template substituting the unfilled stem where the peer's wrong value belongs.

'before reaching 0' is ambiguous: the subtraction that produces 0 is itself one of the subtractions. All three keys are right on the intended reading, but seed 11 hinges on exactly this off-by-one (claim '10 times', truth 9, literal reading 8). A near-miss trap built on an ambiguous phrase is a bad trap.

'This array' points at a picture the text does not contain; the stem states both the total and the row count so no array is needed; two of four options (4 and 8) exceed the stated total of 3 squares and can be eliminated without dividing.

Four of ten items are n / n = 1 (two of them the same item twice with reordered options). This degenerate case illustrates neither equal sharing nor group formation and can train a 'the answer is 1' surface pattern.
Only two of the three named division meanings appear at all; equal sharing is absent, objects are absent, and no rendered model appears in any of the ten.
Grade fit acceptable - all quotients sit inside the G2 tables.
